raw_response:
I have farmed a long time, and with only 6.5 mu plus some family labor working off-farm, I will keep this year simple and steady. I will still center the farm on the wheat-maize rotation because that fits my land, my irrigation from the well, and what I know best. I want dependable grain first, so I will put most of the land into winter wheat followed by summer maize. I also grow chili because it brings cash, but it needs more watching, more pesticide sprays, and more hand labor, so I will only keep a smaller area in chili that I can still manage well. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate fertilizer, and a few irrigations to protect yield without overspending. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because the return is better and it responds well when I have water available. For chili, I will use better seed, higher potassium, and more crop protection because that crop is more sensitive and I grow it for income, not just for grain security. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical on my small plots and matches how I usually manage residue and sowing.
